verdicts.summary: Lean uses a different formula here. Of the four clauses, only the azimuthal one has a counterpart, and it is pointwise rather than an L^∞ norm. AngularGrowth, proved for the constructed field by selectedVelocity_angularGrowth, says |τ^A u_θ(1-τ, ray) - e₀| ≤ C τ^{2h} with e₀ > 0 at the single fixed similarity radius X = innerRadius (ray X τ is the circle z = 0, r = √(2Xτ)); with A = 1/2 + h that is a two-sided u_θ ≍ τ^{-1/2-h} along one ray in the core, which gives the paper's lower bound but not the supremum over C_τ. coreVelocity_norm_at_origin gives the exact axis value ‖u(t,0)‖ = (1-t)^{-A} j for the full speed, again pointwise. Scaling.coreVelocity is only the nominal scale q^{-(1/2+h)} as a definition, with no field attached. No declaration was found stating any of: a supremum over a core region, a rate for ‖u_z^{(0)}‖ or ‖u_r^{(0)}‖, or the ratio bound O(τ^h) — the repository's expansion parameter q^{2h} (slowOrder h n = 2nh) encodes the same relative smallness structurally, but that is a different statement.
